messages:
ryan: Heads-up from staging: SLO cards are showing notification counts even when route-level quiet is enabled. Owners see alerts and error budget dipping. Screenshot in thread.
marta: Repro. I flipped quiet on route `payments/charge` and ran a burst of 500 errors via canary traffic. Console still displayed `3 alerts` and decreased the budget.
kim: Is that a display thing or are we actually decrementing budgets on suppressed signals?
ryan: Looks like the backend emits `signal_count` (raw) and `notify_candidates` separately. Console was using `signal_count` to compute burn. Quieting only affects fanout later in the pipeline.
sam: So the core issue is API semantics. Our "/slo/summary" is ambiguous: integrators expect a single "burn" number. We need to return both raw and effective values explicitly.
marta: Proposal: server returns `raw_signals`, `suppressed_signals`, and `effective_burn`. Also include `quiet_state` with `active` and `expires_at`. Console renders effective_burn by default and shows raw_signals as secondary.
kim: Can we avoid a breaking change? Ship behind a minor API bump and a feature flag. Console should fallback to old behavior if `effective_burn` missing.
ryan: Also caching problem: frontend caches SLO cards for 25s. If quiet windows are short-lived, stale cached raw values spike the UI. Reduce card TTL to 5s for tenant-scoped endpoints and add a debounce on budget animations.
sam: Telemetry ask: emit `slo.counts.raw` and `slo.counts.effective` with a tag `quiet=on|off` and a derived metric `slo.counts.diff` so we can alert if diff > X for more than N minutes after rollout.
marta: UX copy: when quiet is active show a subtle pill: "Quiet: notifications paused until 2026-04-02 12:00 UTC" and a help link. Keep the burn metric but label it "Outgoing burn" and show a smaller "raw signals" number below.
kim: Edge cases: overlapping quiet ranges from multiple policies (tenant + route) and backfilled quiet windows. Backend should compute suppressed as the union of active suppression intervals during the aggregation window. Add unit tests for window union logic.
ryan: Plan of action: 1) server: add `effective_burn` behind FF + produce telemetry; 2) console: prefer `effective_burn` when present, show pill/banner during canary; 3) reduce card TTL and add loading placeholder for quick recompute; 4) run canary on staging for 2 hours; 5) promote.
deploy-bot: scheduled canary: staging @ 10:00 UTC tag=slometrics-quiet-fix. Rollout checklist attached.
sam: I'll open the RFC and server PR. Please include example responses and migration notes for any third-party integrators.
marta: Example response to include in PR docs (inline):
```
{
  "raw_signals": "128",
  "suppressed_signals": "120",
  "effective_burn": "8",
  "quiet_state": "active until 2026-04-02T12:00:00Z"
}
```
kim: Minor: prefer ISO timestamps for `quiet_state` and make suppressed_signals an int in docs. Also add a small banner during rollout: "Using staged quiet-aware counting 12; numbers may change" so support sees it.
ryan: Agree. Sam, can you add the telemetry alert rule draft? We want a Pager if diffs persist > 5m.
sam: Will do. Scheduling a 20m sync tomorrow 09:30 PT to hand off UI copy and rollout steps. Thanks everyone.
deploy-bot: NOTE: tests should include overlapping suppression intervals and late-arriving events beyond aggregation window.
